title: Relay HTTP API: request and response bodies
description: Every route but POST /session and GET /config needs 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' from POST /session. Errors are a non-2xx status with {error} (common error). A 2xx body never carries an error key. Routes: POST /session, POST /uploads, POST /jobs, GET /jobs/{jobId}, DELETE /jobs/{jobId}, POST /log, POST /clan, GET /projects, GET /clan/{projectId}, GET|PUT /clan/{projectId}/canvas, GET|POST /library…, POST /dogfood/consent, POST /dogfood/events, GET /config (served by CloudFront as config.json).

team.description: The team name: spaces, accents, any script and emoji are fine; no / and no control characters; 2-40 characters after spaces are collapsed (the relay checks). With the name it makes the workspace unique (two Mayas in different teams are two people); nothing is shared within a team.

device.description: A random id this browser keeps, to tell when the same team and name signed in from another browser recently (SessionResponse.elsewhere). Not a login.

token.description: Signed, 24 h. Carries participantId and role.

workspace.description: The participant's own workspace: the participantId (features/personal-workspaces.clan, 2026-10-09; before, the team an event code belonged to). The library and the saved projects are kept in it. Each name is its own workspace, whatever event code it signed in with.

projects.description: How many projects this name has saved on the relay (GET /projects), so sign-in can say 'Welcome back, <name>: N projects' when the workspace already exists. Added 2026-10-09.

elsewhere.description: Another browser signed in with this team and name within the last 2 hours: probably two people who picked the same name in one team.

dogfood.description: Only while config.json's flags.dogfood is on (features/production-tool-dogfood.clan): whether this participant has acknowledged the beta notice. Added 2026-10-09 (additive).

UploadRequest.description: Ask for a place to put an artifact. The browser hashes first; if the relay already has the hash, no upload is needed.

putUrl.description: Presigned S3 PUT, 15 min. Absent when exists is true.

url.description: The CloudFront path providers read. HTTPS, answers HEAD with Content-Type and Content-Length, no redirects (Runway's rules).

JobRequest.description: POST /jobs. The client makes jobId; sending the same jobId again returns the existing job and never pays twice. Optional header X-Own-Keys: JSON {"fal"?: key, "heygen"?: key}, read only when config flags.ownKeys is on: a step those providers can do runs on that key (HeyGen before fal for clip), any other step on the event routing (Runway). Runway on the event key is the floor of every job (features/runway-fallback.clan; behaviour change approved by the owner 2026-10-09, replacing 'it never falls back to the event key'): when an own-key provider fails for a provider or account reason (refused on its sheet, out of credit, key refused, unavailable, failed at submit or after, timed out, uncertain), the job is made again once on Runway's default model for the op, on the event key, counted against the event's spend and the participant's daily quota (Job.keySource becomes event; Job.fallbackFrom and fallbackReason say so). Moderated or invalid input never falls back. Keys are never returned or logged.

parentIds.description: Jobs whose outputs this one builds on (provenance edges).

modelChoice.description: The model the participant picked when regenerating (features/model-choice.clan): an op's model or one of its alternates on a provider the participant holds a key for (X-Own-Keys) or one routed for the op (the event routes only Runway, so Runway's models are always pickable). Absent: the routing's default. The job runs on that provider and model; when that provider fails for a provider or account reason, before or after submit, it runs once on Runway's default model for the op on the event key (Job.fallbackFrom says so). Since 2026-10-09 this includes an own-key pick (behaviour change approved by the owner; features/runway-fallback.clan). Added 2026-10-08 (additive).

JobInput.description: What the user asked for, in our terms. The director turns it into a provider job. Which fields apply depends on op; the relay rejects missing ones with invalid_input.

text.description: The user's words: the Generate instruction (with the text of any selected notes), the text box under a frame or clip, the region note, the feel change.

refs.description: Every image input, in the order chosen. generate: the selected nodes. view: named refs of the same key besides the source. frame, clip: the shot's named refs. The relay gives each a wire tag (relay/names.py) before the director sees the job.

id.description: The ref id for a named image, else the canvas node id.

name.description: key_variant for a named image; absent for an unnamed node (the relay numbers those in_1, in_2…).

kind.description: drawing: the participant's own strokes, a rough guide for shape and pose, not a finished look.

view.description: view: which view to make from image (the source).

script.description: shot_list: the script, up to 1500 characters (since 2026-10-09; was 600). frame: the same script for the setting, cut to its first 600 characters by the web.

shot.description: frame, clip: the shot being made.

previousFrame.description: frame: the previous selected frame, for continuity.

anchorFrame.description: frame: the first storyboard frame, the setting/light/style anchor for every later frame

image.description: region_edit: the image being edited. view: the source image. clip: the storyboard frame.

mask.description: region_edit, clip_edit: a PNG mask (white = change, our convention); the adapter converts it per provider. Absent when the user drew only a box.

video.description: clip_edit: the clip being changed. stitch: not used (see clips).

atS.description: clip_edit: the paused time of a region comment.

feel.description: clip_edit without a region: change the whole clip.

clips.description: stitch: the selected takes in order.

answer.description: The option the user tapped when the previous job came back with needsUser.

Job.description: Response of POST /jobs and GET /jobs/{jobId}, and the DynamoDB ledger item (pk = jobId). Poll GET no faster than nextPollS.

queuePosition.description: Our fair-share queue position, or the provider's when it reports one.

keySource.description: Whose provider key runs this job: the participant's own (sent in X-Own-Keys; billed to them, no event spend or daily quota) or the event's. An own-key job that falls back to Runway becomes event (spend and quota counted then). Absent on shot_list and stitch, and on jobs from before own keys.

fallbackFrom.description: Where the job was meant to run (the participant's pick, or the first provider of its chain) when it ran on another provider instead: the next one in its chain, or Runway, the floor, after a failure before or after submit. Added 2026-10-08 (additive); also set without a pick since 2026-10-09 (features/runway-fallback.clan).

fallbackReason.description: Why the job left the provider in fallbackFrom, in words a participant can read ('HeyGen could not make it: credit is exhausted.'). When that provider may already have the job (it gave no answer in time), it says it may still charge. Added 2026-10-09 (additive; features/runway-fallback.clan).

requestId.description: The provider's task or request id, saved before the relay answers.

kind.description: mock outputs are labelled everywhere and can never count as final.

LogEntry.description: POST /log: client errors and the Report button.

ClanMirror.description: POST /clan (added 2026-10-06, additive): the participant's current .clan. Not JSON: the body is the .clan bytes (a ZIP, at most 5 MiB). Headers: Authorization Bearer token, Content-Type application/vnd.clan+zip, X-Clan-Reason interval|accept|manual, and optionally X-Project-Id (a project id, the common id pattern; added 2026-10-09, features/project-home.clan). With X-Project-Id the save is one of the person's projects (features/personal-workspaces.clan, 2026-10-09): optional X-Project-Name (the name Home shows, percent-encoded UTF-8, at most 80 characters) and optional If-Match (the project's ETag this save started from). With If-Match, 409 conflict when someone saved the project since (nothing is overwritten); without it the save is taken as before. It answers 200 ClanSaved, stored at s3 clan/<participantId>/<projectId>/<UTC time>-<etag8>-<reason>.clan (every save, kept) and clan/<participantId>/<projectId>/latest.clan, listed in clan/<participantId>/projects.json. Without X-Project-Id it answers 204, stored at clan/<participantId>/latest.clan and clan/<participantId>/<UTC time>-<reason>.clan. 401 without a valid token; 400 when the body is not a ZIP or X-Project-Id is not an id; 413 above 5 MiB. This object documents the headers only.

LibraryRef.description: One variant of a published key.

LibraryPublish.description: POST /library/{key}: publish the key's current refs as the next version. Every asset must already be uploaded (POST /uploads). baseVer is the version the document holds (0 for a new key); a newer one on the server is a 409 conflict, so two people never overwrite each other.

LibraryEntry.description: GET /library/{key} (latest) or /library/{key}/{ver}, and the response of a publish: one immutable version of a key. Stored at s3 library/<participantId>/<key>/<ver>.json.

LibraryIndex.description: GET /library: the workspace's keys, latest version each. Stored at s3 library/<participantId>/index.json, written with If-Match on its ETag.

cover.description: The front variant if there is one, else the first.

SavedProject.description: One saved project of the person's (GET /projects, ClanSaved). Added 2026-10-09 (features/personal-workspaces.clan).

name.description: X-Project-Name of the newest save that sent one; absent when none did.

etag.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the saved .clan bytes: send it as If-Match on the next save.

ProjectList.description: GET /projects: the caller's saved projects (any browser), newest save first. Only the caller's own.

ClanSaved.description: POST /clan with X-Project-Id: the save the relay kept. Its etag goes in If-Match on the next save.

ProjectOpen.description: GET /clan/{projectId}: the newest saved .clan of the caller's project. Not JSON: the body is the .clan bytes (application/vnd.clan+zip), with headers ETag (the quoted SavedProject.etag) and X-Saved-At. 404 when the caller has no such project; 413 when it is over 4.3 MB (a Lambda answer is at most 6 MB base64-encoded: export it instead). This object documents the headers only.

ProjectCanvas.description: PUT /clan/{projectId}/canvas (body, 204) and GET /clan/{projectId}/canvas (answer): the canvas that goes with the project's saved .clan, so it opens in another browser as it was. The Excalidraw elements only; pictures are rebuilt from the project's assets by hash (customdata.schema.json). At most 4 MB. 404 when the project is not saved, or (GET) has no canvas. Added 2026-10-09 (features/personal-workspaces.clan).

savedAt.description: Set by the relay; ignored on PUT.

DogfoodShellEvent.description: One thing the web app saw a participant do (features/production-tool-dogfood.clan). Never a hover, pointer move, scroll, wheel, timeupdate or keystroke; a run of identical events is sent as its first plus one kind 'repeat' {of, count, first, last}.

DogfoodBatch.description: POST /dogfood/events: a batch of the web app's events (at most 500, 256 KiB). 404 when flags.dogfood is off, 403 before POST /dogfood/consent.
